transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this pre-job review together because we need to discuss the solvent-recovery trial before any authorization is given. As you know, the skid is installed beside the coating area but hasn't been used on production solvent yet, and we have nine hundred liters of solvent mixture in labeled drums awaiting a disposition decision. Before I can authorize this trial, plant policy requires us to conduct this review with process engineering, maintenance, and environmental compliance present. I need to walk through each element of the standard pre-job procedure with all of you: equipment inspection, closed transfer, ventilation verification, vapor monitoring, and documented waste handling. Let's start by hearing from each function on readiness. Process engineering -- can you walk us through the skid's current status and whether the equipment inspection has been completed?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to flag something from my bench compatibility test that I completed yesterday. The results are still in my lab notebook and haven't been uploaded to the process file yet, but they're critical for this discussion. My testing found that only 600 liters of the stored 900-liter solvent mixture is actually suitable for this skid. The remaining 300 liters contains a solvent component that the skid's seals are not rated for. If we run that portion through the skid, we risk seal degradation and potential leakage. We need to segregate those 300 liters before any trial proceeds.

The replacement takes exactly 3 hours, and the seal kit is already in the maintenance storeroom. I recorded this finding on a paper inspection sheet, but it hasn't been entered in the electronic work-order system yet. transcript.text: I need to share my permit review findings, which I received from the environmental office this morning but haven't yet filed with the trial paperwork. My review confirmed that this solvent recovery operation requires three specific conditions: ventilation of at least 6 air changes per hour in the operating area, exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors, and a hazardous-waste manifest for the incompatible 300 liters that Jonas just identified. These are permit-level requirements, not recommendations — we cannot legally proceed without all three in place. The hazardous-waste manifest requirement aligns directly with Jonas's finding about the 300 liters that can't go through the skid; that portion will need to be handled as a hazardous waste stream with proper manifesting. I should note this clarification hasn't been filed yet, so it's not in the trial paperwork the rest of you may have reviewed.
